title_original: Screen International unveils 2026 Arab Rising Stars
excerpt_original: New talent showcase launched in partnership with the Film Committee at Media City Qatar and Doha Film Festival.

blocks.text: Screen International has unveiled the cohort of actors and filmmakers chosen for the inaugural edition of Arab Rising Stars, the new talent showcase launched in partnership with the Film Committee at Media City Qatar and Doha Film Festival.

This year’s selection comprises Kurdistan-Iraqi actor Avan Jamal; Egyptian actor Marawan Waleed; Saudi Arabian filmmaker Lina Malaika; Lebanese writer-director Rami Kodeih; and writer-director Nadia Al Khater from Qatar.

Marking ten years of Screen International spotlighting talent from the region, Arab Rising Stars brings an expanded scope and a refreshed format as part of a long-term partnership with the Film Committee at Media City Qatar and Doha Film Festival.

The 2026 selection was unveiled today (November 20) at the second edition of Doha Industry Days, which brings together leading international and regional figures from across the film and entertainment industries.
The talent took part in a photoshoot at the National Museum of Qatar on November 18, and walked the red carpet at the opening night of the Doha Film Festival on November 19.
E. Nina Rothe, a freelance international journalist and Screen contributor on the MENA region, curated the 2026 edition.

Kurdistan-Iraqi actor Avan Jamal , based in the UK, has appeared in three of Iraq’s Oscar submissions: Shawkat Armin Korki’s The Exam , Sahim Omar Kalifa’s Baghdad Messi and Halkawt Mustafa’s No Paradise If You Are Killed By A Woman.

Egyptian actor Marawan Waleed ’s international breakthrough came with the lead role in Mohamed Hammad’s psychological thriller Safe Exit , which world premiered in Berlin and went on to win the top prize at El Gouna.

Saudi Arabia’s Lina Malaika is a director, producer, film critic, actress and CEO, whose work spans feature documentary One Giant Leap, upcoming survival thriller Red Sea co-produced by Natasha Lyonne, and her role as film contributing editor at Vogue Arabia.
Source: Gareth Cattermole / Getty Images for IMDb
Rami Kodeih

LA-based Lebanese writer-director Rami Kodeih saw his narrative feature debut Furies premiere at the Venice Film Festival, where it secured George Clooney and Grant Heslov of Smokehouse as executive producers.

Qatari writer-director Nadia Al Khater made her breakthrough with 2023 short A Proposal which won a slew of international awards. Her latest project, short Light To Ashes, will have its world premiere at Doha this year.

Arab Rising Stars is a new chapter in Screen International ’s well-established talent initiative that was previously titled Arab Stars of Tomorrow, with a new, long-term partnership based in Doha that will provide a sustained launchpad for emerging Arab talent and continue to connect promising voices from the region with the global film industry.

H.E. Hassan Al Thawadi, chairman, Film Committee at Media City Qatar, said: “Bringing Arab Rising Stars to Doha reflects our commitment to creating lasting opportunities for talent from Qatar and the Arab world and amplifying the voices and stories from our region. Through the collaboration with Screen International and Doha Film Festival, we are supporting our mission to build an enduring, globally recognised creative ecosystem in Qatar. This long-term partnership will provide a platform for emerging Arab talent to continue to shape global cinema. By fostering both cinematic auteurs and innovative new-media creators, we are investing directly in the future leaders of our cultural landscape.”

Fatma Hassan Alremaihi, CEO of Doha Film Institute, said: “Arab Rising Stars is an important new platform to introduce promising regional voices to global audiences. This initiative with Screen International and Film Committee at Media City Qatar reinforces our commitment to nurturing bold groundbreaking talent who are redefining world cinema. By highlighting both traditional and new storytellers, we look forward to celebrating contemporary screen craft from the Arab world and the emerging creatives behind it at Doha Film Festival.”

Matt Mueller, editor-in-chief of Screen International , said: “Ten years on from our first Arab Stars of Tomorrow, launching Arab Rising Stars in Doha represents an exciting evolution. The media landscape has shifted dramatically over the past decade, and expanding our focus to include digital creators reflects how today’s vibrant new generation builds audiences and approaches the craft. With the strategic long-term support of the Film Committee at Media City Qatar and Doha Film Festival, we look forward to spotlighting five exceptional talents who will have the opportunity to define regional and international screens in the years to come.”
